e02d016e0681450b9b4046d09cbeea59.title: Indonesia LPG→CNG Transition under Bahlil's ESDM policy — Q1 2026 (18M)
e02d016e0681450b9b4046d09cbeea59.body: Long-thesis framework for the Bahlil-led CNG-replaces-LPG transition. Five-voice synthesis from Setiawan (regulator), Tanaka (gas markets), Hartono (infrastructure), Pratiwi (end-user), Susanto (macro/fiscal). Independent convergence: 18M target is unachievable at announced scale; realistic addressable share is 8-15% of LPG demand concentrated in Java+Sumatra industrial + commercial gas, NOT households or transport. Investable wedge: long PGAS + HGBT-7 protected industrials (ARNA/MLIA/AMFG), underweight Pertamina Patra Niaga via sum-of-parts. Framework directs human researcher to determine pacing, names, sizing.
e02d016e0681450b9b4046d09cbeea59.key_question: Given the framework's regulatory / gas-market / infrastructure / end-user / macro diagnostics, which 4-6 names earn 3% NAV allocation within 10% gross?
e02d016e0681450b9b4046d09cbeea59.inversion: If subsidy reform (Pillar 1 binding driver) stalls AND HGBT-7 extension lapses, the transition thesis fails — sizing drops to baseline.

744108266b354aa6953fffd5522b4031.title: Driver M1: Subsidy reform — LPG-3kg + CNG subsidy design
744108266b354aa6953fffd5522b4031.body: LPG-3kg subsidy is the single largest non-fuel transfer in APBN's energy bloc (Rp 87.6tn FY2026 allocation, 8.2mn tonnes subsidized volume, implied Rp 10,683/kg subsidy gap vs HET Rp 4,750/kg). The CNG transition lives or dies on whether Bahlil can (a) substitute LPG-3kg with CNG at slower-than-announced household pace, (b) avoid touching LPG-3kg HET (the 2024-25 Permen-ESDM-7/2024 'targeting-only' template — politically safe but fiscally negative), or (c) attempt a 2022-style phased LPG-3kg price reform (politically loud, fiscally positive). My base case: 70% probability Bahlil follows the additive 2024-25 model through 2027; 30% he attempts price reform conditional on post-Pilkada-Serentak-2027 timing. The fiscal-impact arithmetic under LPEM-low assumptions is Rp -5.5tn FY26 / -8.4tn FY27 / -11.9tn FY28 (net negative), vs ESDM-high optimistic claim of Rp +1.4tn / +5.6tn / +10.1tn. Realistic outcome lives between those, biased to the negative side given Pertamina margin compensation, APBN capex absorption, and DMO/LNG-import gas-supply uncertainty. Key institutional veto-point: Sri Mulyani via KSSK; she will permit rollout at 200-400k HH/year pace (not Bahlil's announced 1mn), cap APBN capex at Rp 3tn/year. Disbursement tracks Sri Mulyani's allocation, not Bahlil's claims.

metadata.rationale: Subsidy reform pacing directly governs household jargas/CNG rollout pace (Pratiwi territory)
Subsidy reform timing co-determines HGBT-7 industrial-gas-pricing extension politics (Hartono/Setiawan territory)

90c4a274505a4650951f21eba24adf87.title: Driver M2: Indonesia macro — BI rate / IDR / CPI / Cadangan Devisa
90c4a274505a4650951f21eba24adf87.body: BI policy rate 5.50% (post 17-Apr-2026 25bp cut by Gov. Perry Warjiyo); cumulative easing -75bp from Sep-2024 peak 6.25%. Forward curve prices another 25-50bp through end-FY2026, terminal 5.00-5.25%. BI's revealed reaction function (Warjiyo press conferences) is FX-dominated, not CPI-dominated: 'pro-stability for IDR, pro-growth where headroom permits.' Translation for CNG transition — if subsidy reform leaks USD via CNG-equipment imports (Italian compressors, Argentine regulators, USD-denominated) or via LNG-fed CNG (JKM USD 11.20/MMBTU), BI rate cuts get deferred. Spot IDR Rp 16,485/USD; psychological levels 16,500 (resistance), 17,000 (Reformasi trauma), 18,000 (1998 crisis). DNDF basis vs offshore NDF: -45 to -60 pips, moderate stress vs +/-20 pips baseline. Cadangan Devisa USD 145.2bn (peak USD 156bn Sep-2024; drawdown USD 11bn over 19M reflects active FX defense). Headline CPI 2.84% YoY (back inside 2.5+/-1% target), core 2.31%, administered prices +1.2% (artificially suppressed by LPG/Pertalite freezes — the transmission channel for any LPG repricing). Full LPG-3kg pass-through to economic price = +180-220bp headline shock.

metadata.rationale: BI rate + IDR affect PGN capex financing

Phase-5 (Pratiwi Section 1.2 c): IDR depreciation >16,800 mechanically forces LPG-3kg subsidy line above Rp 100tn even with flat HET; M2 weakness activates M1 reform pressure via subsidy-cost-pass-through

5bf6ea5d95604679807a656186063097.title: Driver M3: Gas supply — domestic vs import dependency (JKM window)
5bf6ea5d95604679807a656186063097.body:
Gas-supply structure is the binding constraint on whether CNG substitutes LPG fiscally-positively (DMO-fed) or expensively (LNG-import-fed). KKKS DMO commitment + Mahakam decline (8-10%/year, Pertamina Hulu) + Corridor flat (Medco) + Cepu associated-gas dependence + Masela (Inpex) FID slipping past 2028 jointly determine whether incremental gas-to-HH supply is domestic or imported. JKM LNG May 2026 USD 11.20/MMBTU spot; city-gate LNG-fed cost Rp 5,600/m3 before distribution vs DMO-fed Rp 3,250/m3. At full 12mn HH FY2030 target, LNG-fed subsidy gap balloons to Rp 8-12tn/year (vs DMO-fed Rp 3-6tn). My LNG-dependency weight estimate: 40-50% by FY2028 — Mei Tanaka arbitrates the exact path. Macro-fiscal impact: at 0.45 LNG-weight, blended subsidy bill is fiscally meaningful (Rp 5-9tn/year FY28) and shifts USD outflow from LPG to LNG (partial offset only). Tanaka owns the detailed bit-supply / cost-stack analysis; I price the fiscal expected-value using the blended weight. Critical macro-tripwire: if Masela slips to 2029+, the entire 'fiscal savings' thesis collapses.

Phase-5 LNG-dependency weight update (Tanaka + Pratiwi joint): mid-case weight updated from pre-Phase5 35-45% (M3 fill assumption) to 40-48% post-Phase5 reconciliation (Tanaka balance + Pratiwi industrial fuel-switch demand overlay). BEAR Masela slip widens to 50-55%.

Phase-5 Masela milestone split (Iwan CONFLICT 1, Tanaka §1.1 correction 2): distinguish two milestones with separate slip risk: (a) Inpex Board FID target 2026-2027 with slip risk to 2028 (probability of slip ~0.35 base case); (b) Masela first-gas target 2030 with slip risk to 2031-2032 (probability of slip ~0.45 base case given FPSO procurement + Maluku infrastructure dependencies). The 18M-horizon thesis only directly depends on FID milestone; first-gas slip materializes in 5-7y horizon but begins to be priced 12-18m ahead of expected first-gas date.

metadata.rationale: Macro-level gas-supply mix directly fingerprints Tanaka's industry-level DMO/LNG cost-stack
DMO availability gates HGBT-7 industrial-pricing extension viability post-2027
M3 LNG-dependency weight rebased on joint Tanaka+Pratiwi gas-balance overlay

4308e52041384dbe94bb2139a81b9b35.title: Driver M4: Fiscal posture — APBN deficit + MBG crowd-out
4308e52041384dbe94bb2139a81b9b35.body: APBN 2026 deficit target 2.53% GDP (Rp 616.2tn); revenue target Rp 3,005.1tn; spending Rp 3,621.3tn; energy subsidies+compensation Rp 394.3tn (10.9% of total spending, 1.62% GDP). Primary balance -0.18% GDP. Sri Mulyani's de facto FY2027 ceiling 2.8-3.0% with UU APBN 2026 Pasal 7 force-majeure clause permitting 3.5% in commodity shock. The decisive overlay: Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) — FY2026 Rp 71tn, FY2027 indicative Rp 120tn (Bappenas RKP-2027 draft, 80mn beneficiaries), FY2028 full coverage Rp 185-220tn. MBG is single largest discretionary spending growth in medium-term budget and crowds out everything else. CNG capex Rp 4-6tn/year competes directly with MBG expansion in Kemenkeu allocation room — MBG is political-priority-1, CNG is priority-3 at best. Tax-ratio target 10.04% is delusional (realization ~9.8%); gap closed by SUN issuance (Rp 775tn 2026 plan, 62% H1) + Danantara dividend. Danantara extracts 5% dividend payout from PGN — directly counter to absorbing CNG capex on PGN balance sheet. Likely outcome: APBN absorbs CNG capex (Bahlil wins), Danantara retains PGN dividend (Rosan wins), Sri Mulyani pays deficit cost.

metadata.rationale: Fiscal posture governs whether PGN absorbs CNG capex (dilution path) or APBN absorbs (deficit path)
Phase-5 (Pratiwi Section 1.2 b): Fiscal capex deferral to PGN balance sheet directly delays jargas SR target for Decile 5-7 households; M4 fiscal stress transmits to I4 execution pace

572ddc9dd8e5495ba9df4dde92e83634.body: Indonesia's CA-balance + IDR are commodity-cycle bound — CPO + coal + nickel determine whether CA stays in the -1% to +0.5% GDP corridor. Composite Indonesia ToT index (BI/BPS Mar 2026) 102.1 (2020=100), down from peak 119 Q3 2022, steady-state. CPO MPOB May 2026 Rp 13,200/kg, USD 935/MT FOB Belawan — stable narrow range. Coal Newcastle USD 122/MT vs FY2026 budget assumption USD 130 (bearish surprise risk for CA). Nickel LME USD 16,800/MT (Indonesia's price-taker problem post-2024 oversupply, Class-1 premium collapsed). Tin USD 32,400/MT. The macro-risk vector for CNG transition is the TOT-to-IDR-to-fiscal feedback loop: if CPO and coal both correct -20%+ in 2H 2026 (CPO on European biofuel demand softness; coal on China steel weakness + policy), CA-deficit widens to -1.4% GDP — that's the 'IDR break 17,000' trigger. CNG-thesis equity-positive case requires TOT staying stable or improving; commodity downside is the dominant ex-CNG macro risk for the long thesis.

5f3e17433cb542199c394b4aa68696f4.title: Mechanic I1: Gas supply & LNG/CNG cost-of-supply
5f3e17433cb542199c394b4aa68696f4.body: Indonesia gas supply is structurally balanced-to-tight, NOT in obvious surplus. 2026 domestic gas balance estimate: gross production 5,900-6,200 mmscfd less ~400 mmscfd lifting/own-use less ~1,300-1,500 mmscfd LNG export commitments leaves ~4,200-4,400 mmscfd available; firm domestic demand (power 1,750 + industrial 1,600 + fertilizer 900 + jargas/transport 35) totals ~4,285 mmscfd. Net balance: -100 to +115 mmscfd, i.e., on a knife edge. The 'plenty of domestic gas' narrative conflates 30+yr reserves with flowing committed supply; Mahakam declines ~7-9%/yr, Tangguh flat, Masela first-gas not before 2030. The CNG cost stack splits three scenarios: (A) domestic-pipe-fed (Corridor->SSWJ->Java) lands at $11.80-16.00/MMBtu wellhead-to-pump = Rp 10,500-13,000/kg CNG; (B) LNG-regas-fed (Bontang/Tangguh FOB -> FSRU Jawa/Lampung -> CNG conversion) lands at $14.80-19.00/MMBtu = Rp 14,500-18,000/kg; (C) JKM-spot-imported lands at $16.50-27.70/MMBtu = Rp 14,000-23,300/kg. Against alternative-fuel anchors at consumer point-of-sale: subsidized LPG-3kg HET at Rp 4,750/kg = Rp 103/MJ (the structural anchor); subsidized Pertalite Rp 10,000/L = Rp 313/MJ; unsubsidized Bright Gas 12kg Rp 17,000-20,000/kg = Rp 370-435/MJ. The arithmetic: NO CNG cost stack - domestic, LNG-regas, or imported - closes against subsidized LPG-3kg without (a) a comparable household-gas subsidy OR (b) elimination of the LPG-3kg subsidy. Against unsubsidized Bright Gas, CNG-via-domestic-pipe at Rp 210-290/MJ is dominant by 30-50%. JKM mid-2026 reads $10.50-11.50/MMBtu front-month vs Bontang FOB ~$9.50-11.00/MMBtu Brent-slope - roughly parallel, no strong arbitrage either way; this is the rare benign external pricing window 2026-2028 that Bahlil's program is exploiting. By 2029-2030, either Masela starts up structurally expanding supply or JKM volatility returns and politics reasserts. The base-case CNG supply mix is 55-65% domestic / 35-45% LNG-import - Aktual's 'CNG repeats LPG import dependency' warning is mechanistically wrong (Indonesia has the reserves) but risk-shaped correctly (without Trans-Java pipeline + East-Indonesia upstream incentive, marginal CNG supply defaults to FSRU regas at JKM-linked pricing that does not close).

8c5baab17ed741369aeaf4d0b5ffab31.title: Mechanic I2: PGN midstream + SPBG/jargas execution
8c5baab17ed741369aeaf4d0b5ffab31.body: PGN (PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk, ticker PGAS IJ; 56.96% Pertamina-owned via Subholding Gas since the 2018 Pertagas-PGAS integration and the 2021 SubHolding clarification) is the operational chokepoint of the entire LPG->CNG transition. The midstream + downstream stack that PGN controls: ~12,000+ km transmission and distribution pipeline backbone (West Java, East Java, North Sumatra dominated), ~835k jargas SR connections at end-2024 (Jokowi-era 10M-by-2025 target abandoned at ~8% completion), ~50-70 SPBG stations nationwide down from ~80 peak in 2014 with most concentrated Jabodetabek + Surabaya at 20-40% utilisation, and ~30-50 mother-daughter virtual-pipeline CNG units serving industrial customers. The Bahlil announce-then-Permen-then-execution gap is the real constraint: PGN cannot legally expand wilayah niaga without BPH Migas decree, cannot build new jargas SR without APBN line approval from DJA / Kemenkeu, and cannot run industrial CNG below HGBT-7 floor without explicit Permen ESDM cover. The internal Pertamina politics that the press misses: Patra Niaga (LPG/fuels subholding) is structurally short the transition (LPG-3kg volume loss + retail margin compression), Gas SubHolding (PGN + Pertagas + Gagas) is structurally long, and the consolidation P&L netting is governed by KBUMN + Danantara strategic allocation rather than market competition. Realistic 18M rollout math (mid-2026 -> end-2027): jargas SR adds 100-200k (vs Bahlil's implied 1M/year), SPBG adds 5-15 stations (vs 3000-5000 target = 30-50x infeasible in 18M), industrial CNG retail volume +20-40% on HGBT-7 extension. The binary swing variable is whether the Permen ESDM operationalising LPG->CNG gives PGN monopoly wilayah niaga (fast deployment, anti-competitive risk) or open-tenders to private CNG operators (Surya Energi Indotama, Energasindo - slow but market-disciplined).

bc3c730e957d4fe6ac2c1a465cd7178f.title: Mechanic I3: HGBT-7 industrial gas pricing (the 18M lever)
bc3c730e957d4fe6ac2c1a465cd7178f.body:
HGBT (Harga Gas Bumi Tertentu, 'specific gas price') is the regulated capped industrial gas price set under Perpres 121/2020 and its operational Kepmen ESDM (Kepmen ESDM 134/2021 and subsequent revisions including Kepmen ESDM 91/2023 covering the 2024-2024-end window; the current Permen ESDM 22/2024 governs 2025-onward implementation). The 'HGBT-7' shorthand refers to the USD 7/MMBtu downstream cap for 7 designated industrial sectors: fertiliser (pupuk), petrochemical, oleochemical, steel, ceramic, glass, and pulp-and-paper (plus rubber-glove for the 2023-2024 extension). The cap operates by forcing upstream gas producers (KKKS) to deliver to PGN/Pertagas at a regulated 'harga di kepala sumur' (wellhead price) of ~USD 4-5/MMBtu, which after transport + distribution overhead lands at USD 6-7/MMBtu to industrial users vs the non-HGBT market price of USD 9-13/MMBtu. The DPMG (deemed-production margin guarantee) mechanism partially compensates upstream for the wellhead-price discount, but this is itself APBN-budget-line dependent and has historically been Rp 4-6tn / year. HGBT-7 expiry is the single most important regulatory date in the 18M Bahlil window: the previous Perpres extended HGBT through end-2024, Permen ESDM 22/2024 operationalised 2025-2027 with cap recalibration to USD 6.5-7.0/MMBtu and the explicit option to add CNG-converted industrials to the protected list. The review cycle that determines 2027+ continuation runs through Q3 2026 (technical review by Dirjen Migas) and Q4 2026 (Kemenko Perekonomian + KSSK signoff) - i.e., INSIDE the 18M Bahlil window. Beneficiary economics: a USD 7/MMBtu cap vs USD 11/MMBtu market spread is a structural ~USD 4/MMBtu margin gift to industrial users; ARNA (ceramic), MLIA (glass-ceramic), INKP/TKIM (pulp), TPIA (petrochem), KRAS (steel) all rely on HGBT-7 for downstream margin. The political risk: Sri Mulyani KSSK has signalled fiscal-discipline scepticism about extending HGBT-7 indefinitely given Rp 4-6tn/yr DPMG cost; Bahlil needs to package HGBT-7 extension with LPG->CNG narrative to clear KSSK pushback.

Phase-5 HGBT-7 canonical reconciliation (Tanaka top-priority, Iwan CONFLICT 3, Pratiwi Section 8.3): Permen ESDM 22/2024 sets the city-gate downstream cap at USD 6.5-7.0/MMBtu (USD 7.0/MMBtu ceiling for the 7 designated sectors); wellhead price is USD 4-5/MMBtu; the DPMG (Dana Pembiayaan Migas, Rp 4-6tn/yr APBN line) bridges the wellhead-to-cap delta. Pre-2024 the operative reference was the USD 6.0/MMBtu floor from Perpres 121/2020 + Kepmen 134/2021; post-2024 the operative number is the USD 7.0/MMBtu ceiling. Iwan's I3 USD 6.5-7.0 figure references the current ceiling band; Pratiwi's I5 + ARNA-root USD 6.0 figure references the pre-2024 floor. Both are correct in their windows but the operative number for 18M-horizon thesis is USD 7.0 ceiling.

4e76defdaf5147c6a8a90b8e5ceb40b5.title: Mechanic I4: Household jargas rollout pace
4e76defdaf5147c6a8a90b8e5ceb40b5.body: Jargas (jaringan gas kota - city gas distribution) is the household-side workstream of the Bahlil LPG->CNG transition. The structural reality: end-2024 base of ~835k SR (Sambungan Rumah) connections nationwide, against the abandoned Jokowi-era 10-million-by-2025 target. The 17-year program (started 2009 under Permen ESDM jargas framework) has missed every target. Reasons: (a) capex per SR Rp 8-12 million substantially APBN-funded historically; for 4M new connections in 3 years APBN would need ~Rp 32-48 trillion over 3 years (4-5x the historical pace); (b) right-of-way (ROW) and land-acquisition issues with Pemda for last-mile pipe; (c) PGN reluctance to expand into commercially unprofitable territories without explicit subsidy or wilayah niaga assignment via BPH Migas; (d) consumer hesitancy from LPG-cylinder familiarity + perceived safety risk + the historical Surabaya 2010s episode of pressure drops during peak. The Bahlil framing implies a realistic 18M target of perhaps 950k-1.05M cumulative SR (i.e., 115-215k new in 18M), which is 4-6x more than historical pace (~50k/yr 2020-2024) but 5x less than rhetoric. Realistic 2027-2030 target if execution accelerates: 4-6 million SR (vs the abandoned 10M). The implementation chain is: Permen ESDM specifies jargas target -> BPH Migas issues tariff + wilayah niaga decree -> APBN allocates capex line via DJ Migas -> Pertamina-PGN board approves capex at RUPS -> PGN procures and contracts construction -> construction 6-12 months per region -> commissioning -> billing. Each link is a regulatory veto-point. The single biggest underrated risk is APBN capex line: if FY27 RAPBN (published August 2026) allocates <Rp 5tn for jargas capex, the 18M Bahlil target is dead on arrival regardless of any other variable. The Bagasmara Madura warning is the regional-political risk overlay: gas produced in Madura must include local-allocation (kuota lokal) provision in any Permen, or DPRD will block.

78d16a3bc70b4fe0a13bea1ae60a2e07.title: Mechanic I5: Transport BBG / industrial fuel-switch demand
78d16a3bc70b4fe0a13bea1ae60a2e07.body: Mechanic I5 (Transport BBG / industrial fuel-switch demand) decomposes into TWO structurally distinct workstreams whose 18M outlooks point in opposite directions, and the framework must price them separately. (A) Transport-CNG (BBG / Bahan Bakar Gas) is LARGELY DEAD per the 2014-2018 autopsy: (1) TransJakarta CNG fleet peaked ~669 articulated + single buses 2014-2016 and has since fallen to ~270 of 4,000+ operational units; the remaining CNG fleet is in run-off as TJ executes 100%-electric mandate by 2030 (Pergub DKI 90/2021), BYD K9 + VKTR Higer deliveries already replacing Hino/Mercedes retrofit-CNG units; (2) Blue Bird Group BBG-converted Toyota Limos collapsed from ~6,500 (2014) to ~2,800 (2017) to effectively zero (2024), rolled back because SPBG queue times 35-50 min + range halving (450 km gasoline -> 180 km CNG) destroyed driver setoran economics; BIRD's stated 2023-2024 fleet trajectory is HEV (Corolla Cross) + BEV (BYD e6) with explicit CNG-skepticism rooted in the 2014-2018 experience; (3) Bajaj BBG (~14k units in DKI) is the lone partial success - stuck because (a) mandate + ban + no alternative + fixed urban radius eliminated the range-anxiety failure mode - but the segment is in secular decline as Gojek/Grab displace tuk-tuk in Jakarta. National SPBG count ~52 stations (KESDM 2024 directory); Bahlil's 3,000-5,000 SPBG ambition implies a 60-100x expansion in 18M against an infrastructure layer that has stagnated since 2016 - infrastructurally + financially infeasible (IDR 100T+ capex to reach even half the headline target). The five 2014-2018 failure modes (refueling friction, range halving, kit reliability ~12-18% 24-month failure, disappearing two-fuel cost differential, Pertamina-PGN turf war) have not been structurally fixed; the EV-policy bandwidth (LCEV roadmap Permenperin 6/2023) has captured all available fuel-switch subsidy capacity. Transport-segment CNG net new adoption in 18M: essentially zero (excluding residual TJ + bajaj). (B) Industrial fuel-switch IS the 18M lever, but it isn't really 'CNG' - it's pipeline gas + virtual-pipeline CNG-by-truck to industrial customers off the trunk pipeline. Economics: HGBT-7 industrial gas at USD 6/MMBtu (Permen ESDM 7/2024) beats HSD at USD 26/MMBtu and MFO at USD 18-22/MMBtu by 3-4x; industrial pipeline gas at commercial USD 8-10.5/MMBtu still beats HSD/MFO by 2-3x. The realistic industrial volume that switches in 18M is 80-150 MMscfd net new (ceramics + glass topped out, textile in distress / unable to capex, cement low-fit, pulp/paper already done) - NOT the 250-400 MMscfd bullish-side thesis implies. The clean listed-name beneficiaries of THIS workstream are the HGBT-7-protected industrial gas-users (ARNA / MLIA / AMFG / KIAS / fertilizer) whose margins depend on the HGBT-7 program extending at USD 6/MMBtu cap. Framework's I5 reading: transport-CNG is a zero-or-negative read on adoption-layer; industrial fuel-switch is a moderate-positive read worth 80-150 MMscfd PGN volume + margin protection for 4-6 HGBT-7 industrials. The conflation of these two workstreams in consensus framing is the single biggest mispricing in the LPG-CNG thesis.

41b82ec9aacf45abb187c007cdcd1e01.title: Perusahaan Gas Negara (PGAS) — anchor candidate
41b82ec9aacf45abb187c007cdcd1e01.body: PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (PGAS IJ, 'PGN') is the cleanest single-instrument expression of Indonesia's gas-downstream transition: 56.96% Pertamina-owned via Subholding Gas (post-2018 Pertagas integration, post-2021 SubHolding clarification, post-2024 Holding Migas restructuring placing Pertamina under Danantara), listed on IDX. Asset stack: ~12,000+ km transmission and distribution pipeline backbone concentrated West Java / East Java / North Sumatra; ~835k jargas SR connections end-2024; ~50-70 SPBG stations + ~30-50 mother-daughter virtual-pipeline CNG units; LNG regasification (FSRU Lampung + Arun + Bali Benoa); upstream gas (Saka Energi); gas trading (Pertagas Niaga); CNG retail (Gagas). Revenue mix (FY24 base): industrial gas distribution ~55-60% (HGBT-7-protected sectors + non-HGBT), transmission tariff ~15-20%, jargas household ~3-5%, LNG regasification + trading + upstream + Gagas CNG retail balance. The framework's PGAS thesis is: subsidy reform progress (M1) -> HGBT-7 extension (I3) -> PGN industrial gas volume + margin -> PGAS revenue / earnings re-rate. The transmission is direct: HGBT-7 USD 7/MMBtu cap delivers PGN ~USD 1.5-2.5/MMBtu distribution margin against ~430-470 BBtud industrial throughput = the dominant earnings driver. Secondary leg: jargas SR ramp (I4) at 50-75k/quarter pace + APBN capex reimbursement. Tertiary: SPBG retail at low utilisation (stranded-asset risk if transport-BBG conversion fails). IDR-USD exposure: PGN bills industrial customers in USD (per HGBT-7 architecture); reports in IDR; ~60-70% USD-linked revenue against ~50% IDR COGS = positive IDR-translation gearing on weakness. Capex FY25-FY26 directed at: M14 / M15 / M14W refinery LNG infrastructure (rather Pertamina-consolidated); PGN-specific Rp 6-10tn / year on jargas + distribution + LNG regas. 9f26225f6de34b2f935d6cd5ac2320b5.title: Synthesis: Perusahaan Gas Negara captures the chain
9f26225f6de34b2f935d6cd5ac2320b5.body: PGAS is the single asset that mechanically converts the framework's full chain into reported earnings: M1 subsidy-reform progress -> I3 HGBT-7 extension -> PGN industrial gas volume + margin -> PGAS revenue / EPS / dividend re-rate, with I2 (PGN midstream execution) and I4 (jargas household pace) as parallel-supporting legs and M2 (Indo macro) + M4 (fiscal posture) as the cycle backdrop. The transmission is direct: HGBT-7 USD 7/MMBtu cap continuation delivers PGN ~USD 1.5-2.5/MMBtu distribution margin against 770-810 BBtud industrial throughput = the dominant earnings driver (~55-60% of PGAS revenue is industrial gas distribution). Jargas execution at 50-75k SR/quarter adds incremental low-margin volume; APBN capex reimbursement keeps balance-sheet absorption manageable. SPBG retail is the option value (low base, large potential if transport-BBG conversion works). The single-sentence chain: M1 subsidy reform on Susanto 70% additive template -> I3 HGBT-7 extended at Q4 2026 review at USD 7/MMBtu cap -> PGN industrial throughput holds 770-810 BBtud at ~USD 1.5-2.5/MMBtu distribution margin -> PGAS revenue +3-5% YoY at 14-16% operating margin -> PGAS FY26 EPS Rp 100-130 / share at 10-14x forward P/E -> dividend yield 3-5% + capital appreciation. The inversion chain (HGBT-7 lapses) breaks every link simultaneously and is the structural reason PGAS is binary on the Q4 2026 review event.

e41bd9fb35d94c2b8d9ccb2cfc098580.body: PGAS FY26 operating margin bridge: industrial gas distribution margin ~USD 1.5-2.5/MMBtu (HGBT-7-protected segment) vs non-HGBT ~USD 2.5-4.0/MMBtu (market-price segment); blended industrial gas gross margin ~25-32% depending on HGBT mix. Transmission margin ~70%+ on BPH-Migas-regulated tariff. Jargas margin ~5-10% on APBN-reimbursed capex + low household ASP. Trading + LNG regas + upstream balance ~10-25% margin. Consolidated FY26 operating margin base case 14-16% vs FY24 trough ~11-13% (post-HGBT-7 cap reset). Tailwinds: (1) HGBT-7 extension at USD 7/MMBtu cap holding distribution margin steady; (2) IDR weakness at 16,500-17,000/USD with PGN USD-linked industrial revenue translating positively (+0.4-0.6% OpM per 1% IDR weakness); (3) APBN DPMG continuation funding wellhead-price discount (Rp 4-6tn/yr); (4) jargas APBN capex reimbursement keeping balance-sheet absorption manageable. Headwinds: (1) HGBT-7 cap recalibration upward compresses distribution margin USD 0.5-1.0/MMBtu (-2-4pp OpM); (2) imported LNG share rising (M3 risk) raises feedstock cost vs HGBT-fixed downstream pricing = compresses distribution margin; (3) jargas balance-sheet absorption if APBN line cut; (4) Pertamina-PGN internal transfer pricing (Patra Niaga vs Gas SubHolding netting) could pressure consolidated OpM via inter-company allocations.

8e307c6692514298a8d868e0ca74e305.title: Perusahaan Gas Negara - Multiple / re-rating drivers
8e307c6692514298a8d868e0ca74e305.body: PGAS trades at ~10-14x forward P/E (FY26E consensus mid-2026) vs cycle-mid 11-13x and cycle-trough 7-9x - implying the market is paying a modest ~10-20% premium to mid-cycle for the HGBT-protected industrial gas distribution franchise. P/B is ~1.1-1.4x against BVPS ~Rp 900/share - within the cycle-mid band, not stretched. The P/E-vs-cycle frame matters more for PGAS than P/B because (a) EPS swings 2-3x peak-to-trough on HGBT-7 / IDR / volume mix, (b) P/E is the cleaner read on cycle position given the dividend-yield floor. Re-rating drivers: (1) HGBT-7 extension at Q4 2026 review with cap at USD 7/MMBtu lifts structural ROE from cycle-average 11-13% to 13-16%, justifying re-rating from 10-12x toward 13-15x; (2) Indonesia-discount compression as IDX gas-downstream cohort rerates relative to ASEAN peers (Petronas Gas, PTT, GAIL); (3) dividend yield 3-5% providing total-return floor. De-rating drivers: (1) HGBT-7 review uncertainty (the single binary event capable of compressing the franchise premium toward zero); (2) Pertamina-PGN governance overhang (KBUMN + Danantara strategic-allocation politics); (3) IDR-crisis scenario pulling P/E back to cycle-trough 7-9x. Bull case: PGAS forward P/E 14-16x at FY26 EPS Rp 120-145 = price target Rp 1,700-2,300/share (implied upside ~25-35% from current). Base case: P/E 11-13x at FY26 EPS Rp 100-130 = PT Rp 1,100-1,690 (implied flat to +10%). Bear case: P/E 8-10x at FY26 EPS Rp 75-95 = PT Rp 600-950 (implied -30 to -40%). The valuation-framework conclusion: PGAS is paying for HGBT-7 protection at current price, which is rational IF I3 extension lands, but offers limited margin of safety if Q4 2026 review surfaces uncertainty.

3c422c20c31c4758845c0d2bd51f40ed.title: Perusahaan Gas Negara - Capital return policy
3c422c20c31c4758845c0d2bd51f40ed.body: PGAS capital return profile is structurally stronger than upstream gas peers because (a) regulated-margin downstream model generates predictable FCF, (b) Pertamina parent consolidates payout via Subholding Gas dividend upstream to Pertamina (which itself transfers to Kemenkeu / Danantara), (c) IDX-listed governance + Indonesia state-owned-enterprise dividend policy norms (Pertamina-PGN cluster historical payout ratio 45-65%). Dividend yield ~3-5% (vs MEDC ~2-3% and ENRG ~0-2%); historical buyback activity minimal (IDX-listed SOE governance prefers dividend over buyback). FY26 capital priorities: (1) jargas SR rollout capex Rp 6-10tn / yr depending on APBN cofinancing (with APBN reimbursement softening balance-sheet absorption); (2) industrial pipeline expansion in HGBT-protected territories Rp 2-4tn / yr; (3) LNG regasification upgrade FSRU Lampung + Bali Benoa Rp 1-2tn / yr; (4) PGN dividend upstream to Pertamina ~Rp 3-5tn / yr (~50% payout). FY26 cycle-peak FCF base case Rp 8-12tn (vs FY24 ~Rp 5-7tn); supports dividend yield 3-5% + balance-sheet de-gearing simultaneously. The framework reads PGAS as the right total-return vehicle in the P3 candidate cohort: higher dividend than MEDC / ENRG / RAJA, lower capital appreciation than upstream peers in JKM-tailwind scenario, but cleaner risk-adjusted return profile under base case. Pertamina-PGN internal politics (Patra Niaga vs Gas SubHolding netting) is the structural overhang: if KBUMN forces Gas SubHolding to compensate Patra Niaga LPG-margin loss via internal transfer pricing, consolidated payout could pressure.

f532d02c83aa4ef98b9bb3a9bb0fdb32.title: Medco Energi (MEDC) — anchor candidate
f532d02c83aa4ef98b9bb3a9bb0fdb32.body: Medco Energi (MEDC IJ) is the cleanest gas-tilted upstream pure-play in the Indonesian universe: Corridor Block (South Sumatra, ~600-700 mmscfd, ex-ConocoPhillips since 2022, PSC extended to 2043) is the LARGEST single gas feed to West Java via the SSWJ pipeline - i.e., MEDC's flagship asset directly powers the Java industrial + power grid that CNG transition demand will compete with. Senoro-Toili (JOB Pertamina-Medco Tomori, ~270-310 mmscfd, Central Sulawesi) feeds DSLNG (Donggi-Senoro LNG, 2.0 mtpa) where MEDC holds 11.1% equity offtake - dual exposure to domestic redirect AND LNG-export economics. Block A Aceh (gas to local industrial + Arun regas-conversion adjacent) adds ~30-50 mmscfd marginal contribution. Revenue mix FY25E: gas ~50-55%, oil ~35-40%, LNG offtake ~10-15% (DSLNG cash distribution). The MEDC thesis lives at the intersection of M3 (gas supply: domestic redirect vs LNG export) and I1 (CNG cost-of-supply: Corridor is the single biggest piece of the Scenario A wellhead-to-pump stack). The asymmetry: if M3 base case holds (domestic-redirect benign window 2026-2028) AND JKM stays $10-12/MMBtu, Corridor gas clears domestic netback at $7.50-9.00/MMBtu (above HGBT $6 cap, since CNG retail is non-HGBT) which is materially above legacy Bontang Brent-slope economics in the same window - i.e., MEDC OPERATIONALLY BENEFITS from domestic-redirect in this window even though headline framing treats redirect as producer-give. Balance sheet: net debt/EBITDA ~1.5-2.0x post-Corridor acquisition deleveraging; FY26 FCF base-case $400-600mn cycle-peak; dividend yield ~3-4% with sustainable cover. Geopolitical: zero China exposure; PSC-counterparty risk concentrated in SKK Migas + ESDM (positive given Bahlil's gas-tilt). The composite scoring places MEDC top-3 on gas-cycle-leverage (highest among IDX gas names after PGAS), mid on AI/CNG-leverage (transmission-not-direct), top-2 on geopol-discount (clean IDR domestic profile), and mid on valuation (P/E ~6-8x FY26E, EV/EBITDA ~4-5x cycle-mid).

b7c449a69c194b9080c6dd66ce1d59c9.title: Synthesis: Medco Energi captures the chain
b7c449a69c194b9080c6dd66ce1d59c9.body: Medco Energi is the single Indonesian upstream asset that mechanically converts the M3 domestic-gas-balance redirect window AND the I1 CNG cost-of-supply Scenario A into reported earnings, with the LEAST dilution: Corridor's 600-700 mmscfd is ~14-16% of all gas flowing into Java + Sumatra industrial/power grid (the same grid that CNG distribution will compete with), so every Rp/MMBtu of CNG-retail-driven wellhead price uplift above non-HGBT $7/MMBtu transmits ~60-70% to MEDC realized Corridor gas revenue, and the rest to infrastructure middlemen (Pertagas/PGN). The single-sentence chain: M3 gas-balance benign 2026-2028 -> I1 Scenario A cost stack <Rp 13,000/kg with >55% domestic mix -> Corridor non-HGBT industrial gas clears $7.50-9/MMBtu (vs HGBT $6 cap) -> MEDC gas revenue +8-12% YoY at firm netback -> MEDC FY26 EPS +15-25% YoY -> P/E re-rates from 6-8x toward 8-10x cycle-mid. The DSLNG 11.1% offtake adds the M5 commodity-tot Brent-slope yield ($40-60mn/yr cash) which de-risks the gas-tilt with oil-cycle diversification. The inversion chain (JKM spike >$15/MMBtu OR LPG-3kg subsidy expansion) breaks every link: domestic redirect becomes opportunity-cost-loss, CNG demand-pull dies, Corridor revenue retreats to government-direction netback below export economics, EPS halves, P/E re-rates to cycle-trough. Unlike PGAS (which is structurally long DISTRIBUTION volume regardless of cost stack), MEDC is structurally long UPSTREAM netback - the two are complementary in a memory book, not redundant.

70456c95f5f7414ebe36719df1100b6d.title: Medco Energi - Revenue drivers
70456c95f5f7414ebe36719df1100b6d.body: MEDC FY26 revenue bridge decomposed: Corridor gas (~35-40% of consolidated revenue) grows ~8-12% YoY on (a) production stability 600-700 mmscfd, (b) non-HGBT realized price firming to $7.50-9/MMBtu on tight balance + benign JKM window, (c) marginal Java industrial demand pull from CNG-driven secondary demand effects. Senoro/DSLNG offtake (~12-15% of revenue, including 11.1% DSLNG equity cash distribution) grows ~5-8% YoY on Brent slope steady at $70-80/bbl and DSLNG nameplate 2.0 mtpa offtake. Oil + condensate (~35-40% of revenue) grows ~3-5% YoY on flat Indonesian Brent realized + modest production from Block A liquids tail + Singapore Block adjacents. Block A Aceh gas + Senoro non-LNG offtake (~10-12% of revenue) ramps on local industrial demand. Consolidated FY26 revenue growth tracks ~7-10% YoY at base case - moderate, not explosive. The under-appreciated leg is the Corridor non-HGBT industrial gas price uplift via Permen ESDM scope: if HGBT-7 stays industrial-only (base case) AND CNG distribution stays non-HGBT, Corridor can sell to PGN at $7.50-9 while HGBT-fertilizer pays $6 - this $1.50-3 spread is the structural margin lever for any non-HGBT-exempt gas buyer including the entire CNG distribution channel.

0be226453d7a415187551ca879e188f1.title: Medco Energi - Margin drivers
0be226453d7a415187551ca879e188f1.body: MEDC FY26 operating margin bridge: gas-segment OpM ~45-55% (Corridor low-cost production + SSWJ tariff pass-through clarity) is the engine; oil-segment OpM ~30-40% (mature-field LIFR steady); DSLNG offtake yield runs through equity-method consolidation so margin-neutral but cash-accretive. Blended FY26 OpM base case ~38-42% vs FY24 ~30% trough. Mix-shift lever: Corridor at non-HGBT $7.50-9 generates per-MMBtu operating profit ~$5-6.50 (lifting + transmission ~$2-2.50); HGBT-bound industrial gas sales (where MEDC has none directly but the framework anchors the alternative-margin reference) would compress to ~$3.50-4 per MMBtu. IDR translation: Medco is structurally USD-revenue (gas sold at USD pricing) and Rp-cost on some lifting + Rp-cost on local SG&A - every 1% IDR weakness adds ~0.2-0.4% to OpM. Risks to margin: (1) Pertamina redirects Corridor industrial allocation to PLN power crowding non-HGBT industrial customers (compresses realized to government-direction netback); (2) HGBT-7 scope administratively widened to include CNG distribution (Corridor forced to $6 cap on those flows); (3) Brent <$60/bbl (oil-segment OpM compresses ~5-8pp); (4) Aceh political instability disrupts Block A throughput.

84de49a235e94aff93c27b4bfbfddca6.title: Medco Energi - Multiple / re-rating drivers
84de49a235e94aff93c27b4bfbfddca6.body: MEDC trades at ~6-8x trailing P/E on FY26E and ~4-5x EV/EBITDA vs cycle-mid 8-11x P/E and 5-6x EV/EBITDA - implying the market is paying a DISCOUNT to cycle-mid, leaving re-rating optionality. The P/E-vs-cycle frame matters because (a) EPS swings 3-4x peak-to-trough so single-year P/E is noisy, (b) discount-to-cycle-mid captures the gas-tilt premium that consensus hasn't priced in. Re-rating drivers: (1) Corridor non-HGBT structural premium (gas-tilt thesis): if framework reads I1 + M3 correctly, Corridor lifts MEDC structural ROE from cycle-average 12-14% to 16-18%, justifying re-rating from 6-8x toward 8-10x; (2) deleveraging (net debt/EBITDA from ~1.5-2.0 to <1.5x) reduces equity-risk discount; (3) DSLNG offtake yield establishes income-floor that supports higher multiple; (4) Indonesia-Brent geopol-discount compression as Bahlil regime credibly delivers gas-policy. De-rating drivers: (1) JKM spike forces Corridor government-direction redirect at netback below export economics - gas-tilt premium evaporates; (2) Pertamina allocation re-pull from Corridor industrial to PLN power; (3) HGBT-7 scope widening compresses Corridor to $6 cap; (4) Indonesia fiscal accident (Sri Mulyani veto on APBN 2027 jargas line) collapses CNG demand-pull narrative. The valuation-framework conclusion: MEDC is paying a discount to cycle-mid that is structurally too cheap if the gas-tilt thesis is right, and fair-to-expensive if the thesis is wrong - asymmetric re-rating optionality.

2ab127cd073449de8b2b3d05f0d550cb.title: Medco Energi - Capital return policy
2ab127cd073449de8b2b3d05f0d550cb.body: MEDC capital return profile is structurally cleaner than pure E&P peers (ENRG, ELSA, ESSA): post-Corridor-acquisition deleveraging on track, dividend yield ~3-4% sustainable through cycle peak, modest buyback authorization history. FY26 capital priorities: (1) deleveraging net debt/EBITDA from ~1.5-2.0x to <1.5x; (2) Block A Aceh modest infill drilling; (3) Senoro/DSLNG maintenance + workover capex; (4) Corridor PSC renewal compliance investment. FY26 cycle-peak FCF base case $400-600mn at ~38-42% blended OpM and 8-10% capex/revenue intensity - opens optionality for incremental buyback or special dividend if Sampoerna (controlling shareholder) signals capital-return tilt. Dividend policy: declared ~30-40% payout ratio historically, consistent through cycle. Korean Value-Up-equivalent (Bahlil Value-Up framework signaled but not codified) provides modest structural impulse. Comparison: MEDC offers higher dividend yield than Korean/US E&P peers but lower than PGAS (4-5%) and lower than POWR (utility-like 4-6%); MEDC sits in the middle of total-return-friendliness in the IDX cohort. Cycle-peak FY26 EPS x payout could fund 4% yield easily; framework should NOT base-case special dividend but acknowledge optionality.

824f7252115e4041bedee4fab24413ab.title: Energi Mega Persada (ENRG) — anchor candidate
824f7252115e4041bedee4fab24413ab.body: Energi Mega Persada (ENRG IJ) is the high-beta, balance-sheet-stressed gas-leveraged E&P + FSRU history in the Bakrie group portfolio: Kangean Block (offshore East Java + Madura, ~120-180 mmscfd gas operated with Mitsubishi + Inpex minority), legacy participation in North Madura + Sampang + Kangean adjacents, and the FSRU operational track record (Jawa Satu Cilacap predecessor work + Bali FSRU adjacents). Revenue mix FY25E: gas ~55-60%, oil ~30-35%, LNG-FSRU services ~5-10%, marginal others. The ENRG thesis is structurally different from MEDC - it is a TURNAROUND/RECOVERY play, NOT a cycle-leverage play: Bakrie group historical balance-sheet stress (net debt/EBITDA peaked >4x post-2014 oil crash; recovered to ~2.5-3.5x by 2023; FY26 target <2.5x via Kangean cash generation + asset rationalization); equity dilution risk lingers if deleveraging stalls; corporate-governance discount (Bakrie group) is structural. The asymmetry: if I1 + M3 benign window holds AND Kangean gas finds firm domestic netback above $7/MMBtu non-HGBT AND Bakrie completes deleveraging milestone (net debt/EBITDA <2.5x by YE26), ENRG re-rates from cycle-trough P/E 4-6x toward 8-10x normalized - a 50-80% multiple expansion on top of cycle EPS recovery. Conversely, if JKM spike OR Bakrie deleveraging stalls OR Kangean reserve revision pulls 12M production estimate, ENRG enters falling-knife mode. Geopolitical: zero China exposure; partner risk concentrated in Mitsubishi + Inpex (positive). Composite scoring places ENRG bottom-half on cycle-leverage (gas-tilt present but smaller absolute scale than MEDC), mid on AI/CNG-leverage (FSRU history relevant to LNG-import-dependency Scenario B distribution), top-1 on geopol-discount (smallest exposure to global supply chain), and BOTTOM on valuation-quality (Bakrie group discount, balance-sheet stress) - which is precisely WHY the cycle-trough P/E creates re-rating optionality if framework reads turn right.

71048474e41c4cd6aa23d4bc9d4b9e6e.title: Synthesis: Energi Mega Persada captures the chain
71048474e41c4cd6aa23d4bc9d4b9e6e.body: Energi Mega Persada is the turnaround/recovery instantiation of the framework's M3+I1 chain - if the benign 2026-2028 window holds AND Bakrie group deleveraging delivers the YE26 <2.5x net debt/EBITDA milestone, ENRG captures both cycle EPS recovery AND multiple re-rating (governance discount compression) in a single 12M horizon, generating ~50-80% upside vs MEDC's ~25-35% steady cycle-leverage. The single-sentence chain: M3 gas-balance benign + JKM $10-12/MMBtu -> I1 Scenario A cost stack <Rp 13,000/kg with >55% domestic mix -> Kangean non-HGBT industrial gas clears $6.50-8.00/MMBtu -> ENRG gas revenue +5-10% YoY at firm netback + oil-segment stable on Brent $70-80 -> ENRG FY26 EBITDA +20-30% YoY -> deleveraging milestone clears <2.5x -> Bakrie governance discount compresses ~10-15% -> P/E re-rates from 4-6x toward 6-8x normalized. The differentiator vs MEDC is the multiple-expansion-on-deleveraging leg - MEDC is already clean balance sheet so its multiple-re-rating depends only on gas-tilt premium repricing; ENRG has TWO levers (cycle EPS + governance discount) but BOTH have to fire for the chain to complete. The inversion chain (deleveraging stalls OR Kangean reserve revision OR JKM spike) breaks 1-2 links at once and triggers falling-knife mode given the Bakrie-group discount baseline.

38443245426341c9a68216f791914574.body: ENRG trades at ~4-6x trailing P/E on FY26E and ~3-4x EV/EBITDA vs cycle-mid 7-9x P/E and 4-5x EV/EBITDA - a deeper discount to cycle-mid than MEDC, reflecting (a) Bakrie group governance discount ~20-30% baseline, (b) balance-sheet stress overhang, (c) smaller scale + offshore lifting premium, (d) historical equity dilution. The discount is STRUCTURAL not just cyclical - even at cycle peak ENRG won't trade at full cycle-mid multiple absent permanent governance repricing. Re-rating drivers: (1) deleveraging milestone <2.5x net debt/EBITDA by YE26 closes Bakrie governance discount ~10-15%, lifting P/E from 4-6x toward 5-7x; (2) Kangean gas-tilt premium adds incremental ~10-15% on cycle-leverage repricing; (3) Indonesia-Brent geopol-discount compression; (4) optionality on FSRU + adjacent gas blocks (LNG-import infrastructure plays are framework-relevant given Scenario B+C dependency weight). De-rating drivers: (1) deleveraging stall + Bakrie governance noise (acquisitions, related-party transactions, equity dilution); (2) Kangean reserve revision triggers production cut; (3) JKM spike forces government-direction redirect at netback discount; (4) IDR crisis amplifies USD-debt repricing risk. The valuation-framework conclusion: ENRG is the highest-asymmetry name in the gas-tilt book - 50-80% upside if both cycle + governance re-rate; -30 to -50% downside if Bakrie group disappoints. Position-sizing should reflect this asymmetry (1.5-2% NAV max vs MEDC 2.5-3%).

9db70992051d45bbaaca0864d9756405.title: Energi Mega Persada - Capital return policy
9db70992051d45bbaaca0864d9756405.body: ENRG capital return profile is structurally weaker than MEDC and PGAS: no current dividend (suspended through deleveraging period); zero buyback authorization; historical equity dilution at cycle troughs; Bakrie group related-party transaction risk consumes capital optionality. FY26 capital priorities: (1) deleveraging net debt/EBITDA from ~2.5-3.5x to <2.5x (the single most important governance milestone); (2) Kangean maintenance + modest infill drilling; (3) selective asset rationalization (Bakrie group disposals); (4) Sampang + adjacent gas blocks workover capex. FY26 cycle-peak FCF base case $80-150mn at ~25-30% blended OpM - all earmarked for debt paydown, NOT shareholder return. Dividend resumption is structurally a 2027-2028 story conditional on deleveraging completion; even then, payout likely modest (10-20%) given Bakrie group's capital reinvestment culture. Comparison: ENRG offers zero income vs MEDC 3-4% and PGAS 4-5%; the thesis is PURE capital appreciation via cycle EPS recovery + multiple re-rating. Framework should weight ENRG accordingly: high asymmetry, no income cushion, position-sized for downside (1.5-2% NAV max). The optionality to upgrade weight is conditional on the deleveraging milestone clearing - which is also the multiple re-rating trigger - so capital-return upgrade and multiple-re-rating are coupled.

2decb3c97ff94b74ba3d68c14dc5dc28.title: AKR Corporindo (AKRA) — anchor candidate
2decb3c97ff94b74ba3d68c14dc5dc28.body: AKR Corporindo (AKRA IJ) is the diversified downstream petroleum + chemical distributor with three structurally distinct earnings legs that map cleanly onto the Bahlil gas-transition stress test: (1) Petroleum distribution (BBM industrial, marine bunkering, retail-fuel JV AKR-BP via 50/50 with BP plc, ~140-160 BP-AKR stations) - directly exposed to industrial diesel/HSFO demand that CNG/gas pivot would erode; (2) JIIPE (Java Integrated Industrial & Port Estate, 60% AKRA / 40% Pelindo, 3,000 ha Gresik East Java) - captive industrial estate with AKRA-distributed gas/CNG to tenant industrials, integrated multi-purpose port, and long-cycle land-leasing annuity revenue; (3) Chemicals + logistics (caustic soda, ethylene-glycol distribution, AKR-CFM China JV). The midstream gas angle: AKRA holds a Pertamina/Petronas downstream gas distribution joint-stake exposure via JIIPE captive supply (small-scale CNG mother-station + virtual pipeline to tenants outside PGN distribution reach) plus historical SPBG investment partnerships pre-merger - making AKRA the cleanest IDX 'CNG-adjacent' name that is NOT directly inside the PGN/Pertamina Patra Niaga political collision. Revenue mix FY25E: petroleum distribution ~60-65%, JIIPE leasing + utilities ~15-18% (highest-margin segment, EBIT margin ~45-55%), chemicals ~12-15%, AKR-CFM ~5-8%. Balance sheet: net cash ~Rp 1.5-3 tn; FY24 ROE ~16-19%, consistent through cycle; dividend yield ~5-7% with payout ratio 50-60%. The thesis lives at the intersection of (a) M3 gas-supply (JIIPE tenant gas demand depends on Java pipeline + LNG-regas availability), (b) I2 PGN midstream execution (every kilometer of PGN distribution that does NOT get built creates JIIPE captive addressable market — JIIPE's value proposition is exactly the gas-supply security PGN cannot guarantee in Gresik/East Java industrial corridor), and (c) Pak Hartono's binding-constraint reading: if PGN executes at historical 62-71% rate against Bahlil's 30-50x SPBG ambition, JIIPE-style captive industrial estate gas distribution becomes structurally MORE valuable, not less — i.e., AKRA benefits from the PGN execution gap. The asymmetry: AKRA is a hedge AGAINST PGN execution failure and a partial beneficiary of gas-transition demand pull, with petroleum-distribution downside if the gas pivot succeeds beyond expectations. Composite score: top-3 on gas-transition optionality (JIIPE leverage), top-2 on balance-sheet quality + capital-return (net cash + dividend), mid on cycle-leverage (petroleum tail caps upside), top-3 on geopol-discount (clean Indonesia domestic + BP JV credibility). P/E ~9-14x FY26E, EV/EBITDA ~6-8x, dividend yield 5-7%.

Both downstream gas distribution; AKRA has JIIPE captive industrial estate, PGAS has national pipeline — different business models, similar gas-supply dependency. AKRA wins when PGAS distribution under-executes; PGAS wins when execution accelerates. Pair-trade complementary, not redundant.

4f77c0bca1b34783b3472a824c0cab23.title: Synthesis: AKR Corporindo captures the chain
4f77c0bca1b34783b3472a824c0cab23.body: AKR Corporindo is the single IDX downstream name that mechanically converts the PGN-execution-shortfall side of the Bahlil program into reported earnings, while keeping a petroleum-distribution defensive floor: the single-sentence chain reads M3 gas-supply balanced-to-tight 2026-2028 -> I2 PGN midstream executes at historical 62-71% of stated rollout targets (West Java pipeline 85-92% utilized, SPBG count 88-95 vs Bahlil 3,000-5,000 target, land acquisition 14-22 months urban Jakarta) -> Gresik/East Java industrial corridor gas-supply gap preserved -> JIIPE captive-gas distribution + industrial-estate leasing annuity premium intact -> AKRA JIIPE segment +12-18% YoY revenue at 45-55% EBIT margin -> blended FY26 EPS +8-15% YoY -> P/E re-rates from 9-14x toward 12-16x as the industrial-estate annuity gets priced. The petroleum distribution leg (BP-AKR retail 140-160 stations + industrial BBM + marine bunkering) provides the defensive cushion: stable mid-single-digit growth on industrial-diesel demand absent meaningful CNG-fleet displacement in 18M (Hartono reads realistic 8-15% LPG/diesel displacement, not the headline 30-40%). The BP plc 50/50 JV adds governance-discount compression relative to pure Indonesian fuel distributors. The inversion chain (PGN over-execution >85% of Bahlil target + accelerated petroleum demand destruction) breaks AKRA simultaneously on both legs: JIIPE premium evaporates AND petroleum-distribution tail compresses - the rare double-loss scenario. Unlike PGAS (structurally long PGN distribution volume) and MEDC (structurally long upstream gas netback), AKRA is structurally long INDUSTRIAL ESTATE CAPTIVE GAS + DOWNSTREAM PETROLEUM CASH FLOW - complementary in a memory book, hedge profile against the other two.

eeb8ee226a714e39aefd378aa3cf9445.title: AKR Corporindo - Margin drivers
eeb8ee226a714e39aefd378aa3cf9445.body: AKRA FY26 operating margin bridge: JIIPE segment EBIT margin ~45-55% (industrial-estate annuity + captive-gas distribution = scarce-supply pricing power) is the structural engine; petroleum-distribution EBIT margin ~3-5% (commodity pass-through, defensive cash flow, NOT margin engine); chemicals EBIT margin ~8-12%; AKR-CFM marginal contributor ~5-8%. Blended FY26 OpM base case ~9-13% vs FY24 ~8-10% - margin expansion driven by JIIPE mix-shift as the highest-margin segment grows fastest. Mix-shift lever: every 1pp of revenue mix shifting from petroleum to JIIPE adds ~0.4-0.5pp to blended OpM. JIIPE captive-gas pricing economics: AKRA buys gas at industrial-rate from PGN/Pertagas/East Java EJGP at ~$7.50-9/MMBtu non-HGBT (the same lever Tanaka anchors for MEDC Corridor) and distributes to tenants at $10-12/MMBtu, capturing $2.50-4.50/MMBtu distribution spread = the entire JIIPE captive-gas EBIT contribution. Risks to margin: (1) PGN under-prices JIIPE feed (industrial-rate compression below $7.50 unlikely but possible if HGBT-7 scope administratively widened); (2) JIIPE tenant defection on competing gas-supply offer (scenario only if PGN executes Gresik corridor pipeline ahead of schedule); (3) petroleum distribution margin compression on diesel/HSFO commodity volatility (modest, pass-through nature); (4) chemicals feedstock price spikes.

726757d189bd4008891ac8d5bf588d43.title: AKR Corporindo - Multiple / re-rating drivers
726757d189bd4008891ac8d5bf588d43.body: AKRA trades at ~9-14x trailing P/E on FY26E and ~6-8x EV/EBITDA - paying a small premium to IDX downstream distribution cohort (KAEF, MPMX, SHIP) but a discount to JIIPE-pure-play comparable industrial-estate names (DMAS, KIJA, BEST) which trade at 14-18x P/E on annuity premiums. The P/E framing matters because (a) AKRA EPS is split-personality: petroleum distribution is commodity-cycle (3-4x peak-trough) while JIIPE is annuity-stable (1.2-1.5x), so blended multiple should fall BETWEEN the two; (b) discount to industrial-estate cohort captures the JIIPE-mix-shift premium that consensus hasn't fully priced. Re-rating drivers: (1) JIIPE mix-shift premium (JIIPE revenue share rises from 17% toward 22% by FY27) - the blended multiple should mechanically re-rate toward industrial-estate cohort as JIIPE earnings share grows; (2) PGN execution shortfall confirmation (Hartono's 62-71% historical reading playing out vs Bahlil 30-50x target) preserves JIIPE structural premium; (3) BP-JV governance-discount compression as Indonesia geopol-discount narrows; (4) net cash + dividend yield 5-7% supports income-floor and downside cushion. De-rating drivers: (1) PGN over-execution (>80% of Bahlil target) compresses JIIPE premium; (2) petroleum distribution accelerated displacement via faster-than-expected CNG fleet conversion; (3) BP plc strategic withdrawal from BP-AKR JV (low probability but watchable); (4) Indonesia fiscal accident widens geopol-discount. The valuation-framework conclusion: AKRA is paying a fair-to-modest premium against downstream-distribution cohort but a meaningful discount against industrial-estate cohort; the JIIPE-mix-shift re-rating optionality is asymmetric and structurally under-priced if PGN execution gap reading is right.

Dividend policy: declared 50-60% payout ratio with regular special dividends; FY24 total dividend yield reached ~7% including special. 23cb6ad14ea547a5a4389e4a822109a4.title: Arwana Citramulia (ARNA) — anchor candidate
23cb6ad14ea547a5a4389e4a822109a4.body: Arwana Citramulia (ARNA IJ) is a pure-play Indonesian ceramic floor + wall tile manufacturer with 4 operational plants (Tangerang Banten, Serang Banten, Gresik East Java, Mojokerto East Java) and ~57M m2/yr installed capacity. The investment thesis is structurally simple: ARNA is the CLEANEST HGBT-7 protection play on IDX. (1) Gas economics dominate: gas / thermal energy is ~50-60% of ARNA's effective cost-of-goods stack (kiln firing + spray-drying + glaze line + dryer) - the highest gas-cost-of-COGS ratio among IDX industrial names, structurally more gas-levered than INKP/TKIM (already converted, smaller incremental share), MLIA (glass + ceramics blend), AMFG (glass, lower kiln intensity), or SMGR/INTP (coal-dominated). (2) HGBT-7 is the binary policy lever: ARNA buys industrial pipeline gas from PGN at HGBT-7 ceiling USD 6/MMBtu under Permen ESDM 7/2024 (7 protected sectors: ceramics, glass, oleochemical, steel, fertilizer, petrochemical, rubber gloves). Permen ESDM 7/2024 expires Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 with a KSSK review at the Sri Mulyani fiscal-discipline gate; extension = ARNA margin stability through 2030; cap removal OR cap raised >USD 8/MMBtu = margin compression of 200-400bps immediately (gas-feed cost spikes from USD 6 to USD 9-11 = full pass-through to COGS = compression at the GM line). (3) Volume side: ceramic-tile market is consumer-discretionary + housing-led; Indonesia tile demand ~440-510 Mm2/yr, ARNA market share ~17-20% domestic. Competing import threat is Chinese + Indian tile imports under FTA (volume ~80-120 Mm2/yr, mostly upper-mid segment); ARNA mass-mid positioning + branded distribution (Arwana, UNO, AromaGres) defends share. (4) Operational moat: gas+electric blended energy intensity ~9-10 GJ/m2 vs Chinese benchmark 11-13 GJ/m2 (ARNA invested in regenerative kilns Tangerang 2018-2022); kiln-level energy efficiency is the structural advantage that HGBT-7 protection amplifies. (5) Balance sheet + capital return: net cash typically Rp 200-450B; dividend payout ~50-65% historical; FY24 dividend yield ~5-6%; family-aligned (Surya Wonowidjojo family) with consistent payout discipline. Composite score: top-1 on HGBT-7 leverage (cleanest exposure), top-3 on capital return (high payout + net cash), mid on cycle-leverage (tile volume housing-cycle linked), top-2 on geopol-discount (pure Indonesia + import tariff defense). Valuation: P/E ~12-18x fwd (cycle-mid range), EV/EBITDA ~7-10x, P/B ~2.5-3.5x, ROE 18-24%. The thesis lives or dies at the Q4 2026 HGBT-7 KSSK review window.

f75674c7124d49f0ad551fa4f2e9c9ef.title: Synthesis: Arwana Citramulia captures the chain
f75674c7124d49f0ad551fa4f2e9c9ef.body: Arwana Citramulia captures the single-sentence chain: M1 subsidy reform politically forces fiscal discipline at the APBN-P 2026 + RAPBN 2027 review windows (Susanto-domain anchor: LPG-3kg subsidy line IDR 87-92T forces reform) -> the very same fiscal-discipline window puts I3 HGBT-7 industrial-gas DPMG (Rp 4-6T/yr industrial-gas margin gift) under KSSK Sri Mulyani veto pressure; the binary Q4 2026 review decides whether HGBT-7 cap stays at USD 6/MMBtu, lifts to USD 7-8 (partial protection), or removes ceramics from the 7-sector list entirely -> ARNA's gas-feed cost (~50-60% of COGS) is the cleanest industrial transmission of the I3 read; HGBT-7 USD 6 holds = GM 33-36% sustains, HGBT-7 USD 8 = GM compresses 200bps to 31-34%, HGBT-7 cap removed for ceramics = GM compresses 300-400bps to 29-32% on full gas-cost pass-through -> FY26 EPS bridge ranges Rp 30-75 across the three outcomes -> P/E 8-18x outcome-band -> price target Rp 450 / 800 / 1,100. The chain is asymmetric: HGBT-7 holds (60% subjective probability) supports base case; HGBT-7 modified (25%) supports bear-light; HGBT-7 dies for ceramics (15%) supports the deep-bear scenario. The I5 industrial fuel-switch workstream (Pratiwi-domain) provides the demand-side cushion: PGN industrial volume +80-150 MMscfd 18M base case keeps gas-feed reliability for ARNA's 4 plants regardless of HGBT-7 pricing outcome. ARNA's structural moat is energy efficiency (9-10 GJ/m2 vs Chinese 11-13 GJ/m2 - regenerative kilns Tangerang 2018-2022) which AMPLIFIES the HGBT-7 advantage but does NOT replace it. Unlike PGAS (long PGN distribution volume) or AKRA (long PGN under-execution + JIIPE captive gas), ARNA is structurally long INDUSTRIAL GAS PRICE PROTECTION - complementary in a HGBT-7-themed sleeve, NOT redundant with PGAS or AKRA. The single-sentence chain lives at the Q4 2026 KSSK window; everything else is operational noise.

d2e648980cc94a9287f497e934146b21.title: Arwana Citramulia - Revenue drivers
d2e648980cc94a9287f497e934146b21.body: ARNA FY26 revenue bridge: ceramic tile volumes Indonesia ~440-510 Mm2/yr at industry level; ARNA at ~75-85% utilization of ~57M m2 installed capacity = ~43-48M m2 sales volume FY26 base case (+2-5% YoY); domestic + export mix ~92/8 split. Revenue bridge by lever: (1) Volume growth +2-5% YoY on (a) housing starts Indonesia (BPS) tracking +3-5% YoY in middle-income tier (the ARNA mass-mid sweet spot), (b) infrastructure + commercial tile demand from urban renewal projects (Pratiwi-domain transit + housing data), (c) modest export growth Vietnam + Philippines under ASEAN trade. (2) ASP flat-to-+2% YoY: Chinese + Indian import competition under FTA caps ASP growth; ARNA branded distribution (Arwana, UNO, AromaGres) holds mass-mid price; premium-tier (Roman, Granito) competes more directly with imports. (3) Mix-shift toward higher-margin Granito/large-format products contributing +30-50bps to blended ASP FY26. (4) Domestic share defense at 17-20% intact under HGBT-7 cost advantage. FY26 consolidated revenue +4-7% YoY at base case = ~Rp 2.4-2.55T. Bear case: housing cycle weak, utilization drops to 65-72%, volume flat or -3%, ASP -1%; revenue -2 to +1% YoY (~Rp 2.25-2.30T). Bull case: housing recovery + infrastructure stimulus + Chinese imports rationalize on Indonesia tariff enforcement, utilization 85%+, ASP +3%; revenue +8-12% YoY (~Rp 2.55-2.70T). The under-appreciated leg is the structural energy efficiency moat (9-10 GJ/m2 vs Chinese 11-13) that lets ARNA hold price even when Chinese imports discount aggressively - the HGBT-7 cost advantage AMPLIFIES this moat.

3e8764c6fdc743c799ed658b10daac9d.title: Arwana Citramulia - Margin drivers
3e8764c6fdc743c799ed658b10daac9d.body: ARNA FY26 margin bridge is HGBT-7 PROTECTION TRANSMISSION: gas / thermal energy ~50-60% of effective COGS = the highest gas-cost-of-COGS ratio among IDX HGBT-7 industrials. The cost stack breaks down approximately: natural gas (HGBT-7 USD 6/MMBtu) ~30-35% of COGS, raw materials (clay, feldspar, kaolin, glaze chemicals) ~25-30%, electricity ~10-15% (heavy spray-drying + glaze + finishing lines), packaging + logistics ~10-12%, labour ~8-10%. GM math at HGBT-7 USD 6: ARNA blended FY26 GM 33-36% base case (historical 32-37% range). HGBT-7 binary sensitivity: every USD 1/MMBtu rise in gas-feed cost (from USD 6 -> USD 7 = +17% gas cost) translates to ~100-120bps GM compression because ARNA cannot fully pass through to ASP under Chinese tile import competition. Outcome matrix: (a) HGBT-7 extends USD 6 = GM 33-36%, (b) cap raised USD 7-8 = GM 31-34% (200bps compression), (c) cap removed for ceramics OR raised >USD 9 = GM 29-32% (300-400bps compression). Energy-efficiency moat (9-10 GJ/m2 vs Chinese 11-13) AMPLIFIES HGBT-7 protection by ~50-80bps GM advantage vs Chinese competition - but does NOT replace HGBT-7 protection. EBIT margin FY26 base case 18-22% (vs GM 33-36%; SG&A ~12-14% of revenue). OpM bridge tail risks: (1) PGN gas allocation rationing under tight domestic gas supply (volume cut, not price - separate from HGBT-7 lever); (2) electricity tariff revision (PLN tariff B3 industrial review); (3) glaze chemical import cost from IDR depreciation. The single most material margin lever is HGBT-7; everything else is operational noise that swings GM by <50bps.

93b3e108a3f246f6ab96d677619efbb6.title: Arwana Citramulia - Multiple / re-rating drivers
93b3e108a3f246f6ab96d677619efbb6.body: ARNA trades at ~12-18x fwd P/E and ~7-10x EV/EBITDA - mid-range for IDX cyclical industrials but a premium to building-materials cohort (MARK, INTP, SMGR on cement; KIAS on smaller-cap ceramics). The P/E framing rests on three legs: (1) cycle position - ARNA is in mid-cycle housing exposure with infrastructure tailwind, NOT cycle-peak (housing starts +3-5% YoY, not the 2014-era 12-15%); (2) structural premium - the HGBT-7 protection IS an embedded margin premium that the market prices asymmetrically (more weight on confirmation than on tail risk because HGBT-7 has extended at every review since 2016); (3) capital-return floor - dividend yield 5-6% + 50-65% payout ratio supports income-floor on any P/E compression. Re-rating drivers: (a) HGBT-7 extension at Q4 2026 confirmed at USD 6 cap = P/E re-rates to 15-18x cycle-peak range as binary uncertainty resolves; (b) housing-cycle recovery (BPS housing starts >5% YoY) supports +1-2x P/E expansion; (c) Chinese tile import tariff enforcement at >12-15% = ARNA pricing power validated. De-rating drivers: (1) HGBT-7 cap raised >USD 8 OR scope narrowed = P/E re-rates to 8-10x cycle-trough (this is the deep-bear case); (2) housing cycle weak + tile imports surge compound (4-5x P/E compression on housing/import double-loss); (3) Surya Wonowidjojo family payout discipline review (low probability but watchable); (4) IDR depreciation >17,500/USD raises imported clay/feldspar cost. The valuation conclusion: ARNA is paying a fair premium vs building-materials cohort for its HGBT-7 leverage; the binary Q4 2026 review is the single re-rating / de-rating event the market is positioning around. Cycle-mid 12-15x P/E + dividend yield 5-6% gives ~6-8% total-return floor in base case before HGBT-7 confirmation upside.

c08d7601b5ca48c0863fe9feb78a83b2.title: Arwana Citramulia - Capital return policy
c08d7601b5ca48c0863fe9feb78a83b2.body: ARNA capital return profile is one of the cleanest in the HGBT-7-protection sleeve: net cash typically Rp 200-450B (versus modest capex needs in maintenance years), dividend payout ratio ~50-65% historical, dividend yield ~5-6% at cycle-mid, occasional special distributions in over-earning years. FY26 capital priorities: (1) maintenance capex ~Rp 100-180B (kiln refurbishment + line upgrades + minor capacity debottlenecking); (2) optional Mojokerto plant Phase II expansion capex ~Rp 300-500B over 2 years IF housing-cycle confirms recovery + HGBT-7 extends (gating condition); (3) regular dividend distribution; (4) opportunistic buyback within float constraints (Surya Wonowidjojo family controls ~62% so float-constrained). FY26 FCF base case Rp 320-450B at GM 33-36% / EBIT 18-22%; covers maintenance capex + dividend with modest surplus. Dividend policy: declared 50-65% payout ratio with discretionary special in over-earning cycle years; FY24 yield reached ~5.5% with special. Family alignment: Surya Wonowidjojo family payout discipline historically high - dividend is the family's primary cash extraction mechanism, structurally stable. Comparison among HGBT-7-protection candidates: ARNA dividend yield 5-6% comparable to MLIA 4-6%, higher than AMFG 2-4% (minority float + glass capex cycle), higher than KIAS (small-cap, irregular dividend). The capital-return profile adds 5-6% to total-return floor regardless of HGBT-7 binary outcome - the dividend yield IS the structural floor on de-rating scenarios; in deep-bear case where P/E re-rates to 8-10x, dividend yield would compress to 4-5% but remain meaningful.

81fa2ec772fc44e390dcde1271fb8804.body: BEAR envelope (probability 0.30, 18M horizon): Subsidy reform stalls AND commodity weak. Sri Mulyani vetoes DPMG expansion at Q4 2026 KSSK review (APBN deficit >3% pressuring FY27 tightening); HGBT-7 cap recalibrated >USD 7.5/MMBtu OR scope narrowed (ceramics dropped from 7-sector list); jargas APBN line cuts from Rp 3-5tn toward Rp 1-2tn (MBG overshoot to Rp 130-150tn vs Rp 110tn base crowds out energy capex); Masela FID slips to 2028 with first-gas deferred to 2031-2032; CPO+coal joint TOT collapses -20% sustained 2M (China property bid fading + EU EUDR weighing on CPO); IDR breaks 17,000 sustained 30d; commodity-leveraged import cost shock. PGAS revenue flat-to-+5% (HGBT-7 erosion on industrial volume + jargas stall); ARNA EPS -25% to -35% bear case Rp 50 (HGBT cap >USD 8 + housing weak); AKRA EPS compressed Rp 95 (JIIPE growth <8% + PGN over-execution compresses captive-gas premium); ENRG EPS Rp 32 (Kangean reserve cut + Bakrie dilution). JCI -10 to -20% (basket underperforms by 3-8pts). Cohort PT: PGAS Rp 750, ARNA Rp 450, AKRA Rp 850, ENRG Rp 95. Tripwire population: 2-3 unfavorable + 0 favorable firing.

febbefc1049a468ca8966decaaf03bbc.title: Consensus snapshot on PGAS + transition
febbefc1049a468ca8966decaaf03bbc.body: Sell-side consensus on PGAS + the CNG transition (Mandiri Sekuritas, Maybank Indonesia, BCA Sekuritas, CIMB Niaga Sekuritas, Indo Premier; cross-ref Morgan Stanley Asia gas analysts): (a) PGAS PT mean ~Rp 1,800-2,000/share (vs Q1 2026 spot ~Rp 1,580); (b) implied 12M return +15-25%; (c) consensus narrative: 'PGAS is the pure-play CNG-transition winner; Bahlil's Rp 4-6tn capex flows to PGN balance sheet with reimbursement; CNG household conversions accelerate to 1mn/year on Bahlil's roadmap; HGBT-7 industrial pricing extended to 2030 protects margins'; (d) consensus EPS FY26 Rp 168 / FY27 Rp 195 (~+16% YoY); (e) consensus assumption: fiscal-neutral CNG transition. The framework's macro-fiscal reading is materially more cautious — fiscally-negative case Rp 5-12tn/year FY26-28 means Sri Mulyani caps APBN capex at Rp 3tn/year, PGN absorbs the residual on its balance sheet (dilution risk re-emerges), CNG household conversions actual pace 200-400k/year (not 1mn). Implication: consensus PT Rp 1,800-2,000 overstates fair value by 15-25%; framework PT bias is Rp 1,450-1,650 base / Rp 1,800 bull / Rp 1,150 bear.

6da4fba1c9f648b883b377beca72a0c8.title: Market-implied valuation
6da4fba1c9f648b883b377beca72a0c8.body: PGAS trades ~Rp 1,580/share (Q1 2026), market cap ~Rp 38tn, fwd P/E ~9.5x (FY26 EPS Rp 168 consensus). Implied: market is pricing FY26-FY28 distribution-volume growth 5-8%/year, HGBT-7 extension priced as base case, CNG household ramp at moderate (not aggressive) pace, no equity-raising. EV/EBITDA ~5.0x, vs PGN's own pre-2022 average 6.5-7x — implying the market has already digested some HGBT-7-protection skepticism and CNG-uncertainty discount. Dividend yield 6.2% (Rp 98/share trailing) supports valuation floor. Cross-asset triangulation: at 8.0x fwd P/E PGAS would print Rp 1,344 (-15%); at 11.0x Rp 1,848 (+17%); at framework-bear scenario 7.5x Rp 1,260 (-20%); at framework-bull 10.5x Rp 1,764 (+12%). The market-implied option-value embedded — that's the 'CNG-transition winner' premium — is roughly Rp 200-300/share, or 12-19% of current price. If subsidy reform stalls and DMO supply tightens, that option-value compresses to Rp 50-150 (-50% on the option). If reform accelerates and DMO supply holds, option value expands to Rp 350-450 (+50%).

6c4bfb21d1734dc38e63d69064f55521.title: Gap vs framework reading
6c4bfb21d1734dc38e63d69064f55521.body: Framework-vs-consensus gap across 5 macro drivers: (M1 subsidy reform) framework weights 70% additive 2024-25 template + 30% 2022-style reform with Pilkada gate; consensus assumes Bahlil's 1mn HH/year + neutral fiscal — gap is on volume + fiscal math. (M2 Indo macro) consensus assumes BI easing path to 5.00% terminal; framework agrees on direction but adds 25% probability of mid-cycle pause if IDR breaches 16,800 — gap is on the FX-dominant reaction function. (M3 gas supply) consensus implicitly assumes DMO-fed CNG through 2030; framework prices 40-50% LNG-dependency weight by FY2028 — gap is on Masela FID timing + Mahakam decline. (M4 fiscal posture) consensus assumes Sri Mulyani's APBN deficit ceiling holds and CNG capex absorbed in headroom; framework reads MBG crowd-out forces Sri Mulyani to cap CNG capex Rp 3tn (not 4-6tn) — gap is on intra-budget allocation. (M5 commodity TOT) consensus assumes current stable-state ToT continues; framework prices 30% probability of CPO+coal joint -20% correction in 2H 2026 — gap is on Europe/China demand softness. The five gaps cluster around 'consensus assumes Bahlil's narrative is delivered' vs 'framework assumes Bahlil's narrative is partially delivered, slowly, under Sri Mulyani veto'.

metadata.rationale: Gap on M1: framework prices 30% probability 2022-style reform vs consensus base case additive template
Gap on M2: framework prices 25% mid-cycle pause vs consensus straight-line easing to 5.00%

74da30b2f19f4d11b76281a7c3ec9e77.body: Positioning across the Indonesian-equity macro funnel: (a) MSCI Indonesia weight in MSCI EM ~1.7% (mid-decade trough; vs 2.4% pre-2022 normalization); (b) foreign ownership of SUN 14.2% (vs >25% pre-2022, resilience higher); (c) foreign ownership of IDX equity bloc ~31-33% (compressed from 40%+ in 2018); (d) PGAS foreign ownership ~14-18%, modest; (e) short interest on PGAS ~0.4% float (negligible — no short-covering cushion in selloff); (f) SUN-yield-driven IDR proxy ETFs (IDX-MSCI EM share) show modest net-buy; (g) BMRI / BBRI MSCI ACWI EM-Index weighting ~50bp each — passive flow vulnerability. Implication: positioning has already discounted much of the 2022-24 EM-stress, leaving Indonesian equity less crowded than 2022 peak. The macro-positioning thesis: the lighter positioning means a CNG-transition delivery surprise (consensus-friendly outcome) prints meaningful PGAS upside without crowded-trade unwind risk; conversely, a fiscal-stress surprise still triggers EM-redemption-driven outflow that hits PGAS via index passivity not specific-fundamentals.

585684a7972f40d683c8b640b066ada4.title: Narrative — Bahlil delivers vs Bahlil overpromises
585684a7972f40d683c8b640b066ada4.body: Two competing narratives drive the 18M tape: (1) Street narrative — 'Bahlil delivers: 1mn HH/year CNG conversion, APBN absorbs Rp 4-6tn capex, fiscal-neutral outcome, HGBT-7 extended to 2030, PGAS the pure-play winner; Indonesia executes on energy transition'; (2) Framework counter-narrative — 'Bahlil announces, Sri Mulyani caps, Pertamina compensates; actual delivery 200-400k HH/year; fiscally-negative Rp 5-12tn/year; PGN balance sheet absorbs residual capex (dilution risk re-emerges); CNG transition becomes a 5-10 year arc, not 18M.' A third narrative — 'Bahlil reshuffled late-2026 cabinet adjustment; CNG program paused; LPG targeting-only model returns' — carries 15-20% probability and is the framework's tail scenario. The narrative gap is binary on the delivery-pace question — both frames cannot be right on 12-18M horizon. Resolution observables: (a) actual CNG HH conversions by mid-2026 vs Bahlil's claim, (b) APBN realization on capex line, (c) Sri Mulyani public statements on subsidy framework, (d) Pertamina-PGN-Kemenkeu MoU finalization. Framework's bias: 60-70% probability Street narrative partially-but-not-fully delivers; 20-25% probability framework narrative wins decisively; 10-15% probability tail (Bahlil reshuffled).

Cadence: weekly review of (a)+(c)+(d); monthly review of (b)+(e); ad-hoc on (f). The framework uses lead indicators to pre-position before coincident prints (PGAS quarterly, BI RDG, BPS CPI) confirm. Specifically: APBN monthly realization deviation >5% vs schedule is the cleanest single lead for fiscal-stress; ICE LPG forward >USD 720/MT is the cleanest single lead for LPG-subsidy line blowout; Sri Mulyani 'fiscal sustainability' mention frequency is the cleanest single lead for behind-scenes CNG-capex veto.

911a7aba6e5f432fa753bad26cccb921.body: Coincident indicators confirm the macro-fiscal regime in real time: (a) PGAS quarterly earnings — revenue, EBITDA, capex disbursement, dividend payout, gearing; (b) LPG-3kg sales volume — monthly Pertamina disclosure; (c) jargas SR (sambungan rumah) additions — PGN quarterly; (d) APBN realization vs schedule monthly; (e) BPS CPI monthly (headline, core, admin); (f) BI RDG monthly rate decision; (g) JISDOR daily IDR fixing; (h) Cadangan Devisa monthly. The framework reads coincident prints as confirmation/refutation of pre-positioned leads. Most important single coincident for the thesis: PGAS Q2/Q3 2026 capex disbursement pace (low = framework right; high = consensus right). Second: monthly LPG-3kg sales volume trajectory (rising = no substitution; falling = CNG actually substituting). Third: monthly admin-price CPI sub-component (flat = subsidy retention; rising = LPG/Pertalite passthrough). Cadence: monthly review of all 8; deep-dive on PGAS quarterly + ESDM Pertamina disclosure.

312a8f24b6d96583c541e107f5e41558.body: Consensus framing conflates the two I5 workstreams: it implicitly weights transport-CNG revival (TJ/Damri/Bluebird/Bajaj CNG mandate) on the same footing as industrial fuel-switch (HGBT-7-protected industrials gas pipeline + virtual-pipeline demand). Pratiwi BBG 2014-2018 autopsy reads transport-CNG as essentially dead in 18M: TransJakarta CNG fleet down from 669 (2014) to ~270 (2024) and trajectory-EV; Blue Bird BBG taxi fleet 6,500 (2014) -> 0 (2024); national SPBG count ~52 (2024) vs Bahlil 3,000-5,000 target infeasible; the 5 failure modes (refueling friction, range halving, kit reliability ~12-18% 24mo failure rate, disappearing two-fuel cost differential, Pertamina-PGN turf war) are structurally unfixed; EV-policy bandwidth (Permenperin 6/2023 LCEV roadmap) has captured all fuel-switch subsidy capacity. Framework reads industrial fuel-switch realistically at +80-150 MMscfd 18M base case (NOT consensus 250-400 MMscfd) - smaller but real, gated on HGBT-7 Q4 2026 extension. The single biggest mispricing in the LPG-CNG thesis is treating these two workstreams as additive when one is dead and the other is binary on a single regulatory event. Listed-name implication: ARNA + MLIA + AMFG + KIAS are the HGBT-7-protection sleeve (live workstream); AUTO/SMSM/BIRD are transport-CNG revival proxies (dead workstream) and any thesis weighting them positively is mispriced.

ee04266d5728a1cafd35d1d058d5139e.title: Synthesis: 18M financing gap Rp 50-80tn for transition program
ee04266d5728a1cafd35d1d058d5139e.body: Phase-5 macro synthesis (Hartono Leak 2): aggregate transition financing requirement vs APBN absorption capacity. SPBG (CNG station) capex Rp 48-55tn (800 stations target x Rp 60-70bn unit cost) + jargas household capex Rp 32-48tn (cumulative 1-1.2mn SR x Rp 27-40mn unit cost incl trunk) + HGBT-7 DPMG bridge Rp 4-6tn/yr = total Rp 90-115tn over 18M horizon. APBN absorption Rp 2-3tn/yr (DPMG line + jargas line + SPBG capex) = ~Rp 3-5tn over 18M. Net financing gap Rp 50-80tn. Consequence chain: (a) PGN PMN injection Rp 20-30tn (Pertamina-PGN-Kemenkeu MoU Q3 2026 critical-path event); (b) target re-baselining (3mn jargas SR target reduced to 1.5-2mn); (c) APBN deficit slip via Pasal 7 force-majeure invocation. This single chip captures the 'where does the money come from' question that pre-Phase5 framework didn't fully synthesize.

metadata.rationale: Financing gap is fiscal stress amplifier
Gap drives PGN PMN injection decision
Gap caps jargas SR pace if PMN not signed
Gap pressures DPMG line first under fiscal tightening

533a1e7e7cb4f251c540c8b302263cbc.title: M4 - Pertamina Holding RUPS Q4 2026 capex allocation Gas-SubHolding share
533a1e7e7cb4f251c540c8b302263cbc.body: Phase-5 add (Hartono Leak 3): Pertamina Holding's Q4 2026 RUPS decides FY27 capex allocation across SubHoldings. The Gas SubHolding share (vs Upstream, Refining, Commercial-Trading, NRE) is the single binary decision event that determines whether Bahlil's CNG transition has internal-Pertamina capital backing. Pre-2024 baseline: Gas SubHolding ~22-25% of holding capex. Target for transition: >30%. Below 28% signals internal politics deprioritizing gas in favor of upstream replacement (Bakrie-adjacent influence) or downstream refining (KOPI 1 + KOPI 2 sustainability).

Gas SubHolding share directly funds PGN trunk + jargas capex

a46da29ff6a24be1b2627230588ff110.title: I2 - BPH Migas wilayah niaga decree for CNG retail (12-18M lag)
a46da29ff6a24be1b2627230588ff110.body: Phase-5 add (Iwan Missing diag #1): BPH Migas (Badan Pengatur Hilir Migas) wilayah niaga (commercial-zone) decree determines whether CNG retail can be lawfully marketed in newly-designated zones. Binary status: issued vs unissued. Decree issuance has 12-18M lag on actual CNG retail expansion (zoning -> permit -> station construction -> fueling). If decree unissued by mid-2027, CNG retail expansion 2027-28 is materially delayed regardless of Bahlil's headline target.

metadata.rationale: Regulatory completeness for retail markets
Decree underpins CNG retail-vs-LPG-3kg substitution path
